land.text: the island of Cyprus, infobox predecessor 'Theme of Cyprus'

predecessors.note: The infobox lists 'Theme of Cyprus; Cyprus under the Knights Templar; Armenian Kingdom of Cilicia' as predecessors. The page says Richard I conquered the island in 1191, sold it to the Knights Templar for 100,000 bezants, and took it back after the Templars were expelled in an Easter 1192 uprising; the Templars have no dossier, so the island is attributed to the Byzantine Empire (the 'Theme of Cyprus'). The excerpt read does not name the Byzantine ruler Richard defeated.

land.text: the island of Cyprus ('Venetian Cyprus', the infobox successor)

successors.note: Lead: Catherine Cornaro, 'the last queen', 'was forced to sell the island to Venice'; the dynasty table ends her reign on 26 February 1489. Claimants section: she ceded her rights to Venice in 1476. Cliopatria keeps a Kingdom of Cyprus shape to 1491.

capitals.name: Nicosia (Lefkosia)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Nicosia'; the page calls inland Nicosia 'the traditional capital' and Famagusta the commercial hub. The page gives no capital move and no year for any coronation at Famagusta.

rulers.name: Catherine Cornaro
rulers.title: Last queen
rulers.note: 26 August 1474 to 26 February 1489; the table gives the name as 'Catherine'.

correction.text: the island of Cyprus; shape unchanged, but it holds for 1192-1360 only (the Anatolian ports are added from 1361)

keyframe_review.note: The page gives the kingdom as 'established by the French House of Lusignan after the Third Crusade' (infobox 'Established: 1192') on the island alone until 'Antalya between 1361 and 1373, and Corycus between 1361 and 1448' (lead, marked citation needed). Cliopatria's shape (11,437 km2, the island plus its coastal waters) stays on the island to 1362, two years too long. The infobox gives no area to compare.

correction.text: Cyprus with Antalya (from 1361) and Corycus (from 1361), the shape Cliopatria draws from 1363

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the lead's 'Antalya between 1361 and 1373, and Corycus between 1361 and 1448' puts the two Anatolian ports under the kingdom from 1361, two years before Cliopatria's 1363 shape. Famagusta is still Cypriot (it is seized by Genoa in 1372).

correction.text: shape unchanged; it belongs to 1361-1371 only (new keyframe kingdom-of-cyprus_1361). Cliopatria keeps it to 1486, 113 years after Antalya (1373) and 38 years after Corycus (1448) were lost

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's 1363-1486 shape (12,653 km2, 46 cells against 18 for the island) includes the Anatolian coast for 124 years; the lead gives Antalya only to 1373 and Corycus only to 1448. For 1372-1486 use the new keyframes 1372, 1373, 1448 and 1464. The infobox gives no area.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Famagusta page, 'In 1372 the port was seized by Genoa and in 1489 by Venice'. A one-year keyframe because Antalya is lost the next year.

minus.text: the port of Famagusta and its immediate district

correction.text: 1373-1447: Cyprus without Famagusta (Genoese) and without Antalya, but still with Corycus

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the lead ends Antalya in 1373 while Corycus lasts to 1448. Famagusta stays Genoese on this keyframe until the bridging year 1464 (see the 1464 gain).

minus.text: the port of Famagusta and its immediate district

correction.text: 1448-1463: the island of Cyprus without Famagusta (Genoese); no Anatolian possessions

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Corycus 'between 1361 and 1448' (lead) leaves only the island, minus Famagusta.

correction.text: 1464-1486: the whole island of Cyprus again, Famagusta back under the king

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, year bridging (confidence 1): the Famagusta page says only that the port was seized by Genoa in 1372 and by Venice in 1489, so it must have returned to the kingdom in between, but it gives no year. 1464 is the year the Kingdom of Cyprus page's dynasty table starts James II; no page opened says he recovered Famagusta.

correction.text: the island of Cyprus; shape unchanged, but the kingdom ends in 1489, not 1491

keyframe_review.note: Infobox 'Disestablished: 1489'; the dynasty table ends Catherine's reign on 26 February 1489 and the lead says she 'was forced to sell the island to Venice'. Cliopatria's 1490-1491 years belong to Venetian Cyprus.

ledger.note: 1192: the Lusignans take Cyprus and found the Kingdom of Cyprus after the Third Crusade. Lead: 'established by the French House of Lusignan after the Third Crusade'; infobox 'Established: 1192'. Richard I 'conquered' the island in 1191, sold it to the Templars, and after their expulsion in an Easter 1192 uprising offered Guy the lordship; Guy died in 1194.
ledger.counterpart: Knights Templar (Cyprus under the Knights Templar, 1191-1192; no dossier)

ledger.note: 1196: the Holy Roman Emperor approves the crown of Cyprus, turning Guy's lordship into a kingdom under Aimery (the dynasty table calls Guy 'Lord' and Aimery 'First king'). The page's wording is that the crown and title 'was approved in 1196'; no territorial change.

1361: the kingdom takes Antalya on the Anatolian coast. Lead: the kingdom comprised 'Antalya between 1361 and 1373' (marked citation needed). The page does not say who held it; the Beylik of Teke is the Cliopatria neighbour (bbox 28.4-32.0 E, touching Cyprus's shape 1363-1428), so the counterpart is the researcher's reading.

region.text: Corycus (Korykos, Gorigos) on the Cilician coast

ledger.note: 1361: the kingdom takes Corycus on the Cilician coast. Lead: 'Corycus between 1361 and 1448' (citation needed). The page does not name the previous holder; the infobox lists the Armenian Kingdom of Cilicia among Cyprus's predecessors and Cliopatria's Cilician shape (bbox 33.6-38.2 E, 36.2-37.9 N) covers the site, so the counterpart is the researcher's reading.

region.text: the port of Famagusta and its immediate district

ledger.note: 1372: Genoa seizes the port of Famagusta. Famagusta page: 'In 1372 the port was seized by Genoa and in 1489 by Venice.' The Kingdom of Cyprus infobox gives 'Tributary state of the Republic of Genoa (1372-1426)' (citation needed). The page gives no month and no terms.
1373: Antalya leaves the kingdom. Lead: 'Antalya between 1361 and 1373'. The page does not say how it was lost or to whom; the Beylik of Teke is the neighbouring Cliopatria state (reading).

region.text: Corycus (Korykos, Gorigos) on the Cilician coast

ledger.note: 1448: Corycus leaves the kingdom. Lead: 'Corycus between 1361 and 1448'. The page does not say how it was lost or to whom; the Ramadanid Emirate (bbox 33.6-37.1 E, 36.2-37.9 N, listed as touching Cyprus's shape 1385-1486) is the nearest Cliopatria state, so the counterpart is the researcher's reading and a gap-filler should confirm it. [Reviewer me-09-d, 2026-10-24] Counterpart changed from ramadanid-emirate: the Corycus page says 'From 1448 or 1454 it belonged alternately to the Karamanids, the Egyptians' and does not name the Ramadanids.

region.text: the port of Famagusta and its immediate district

ledger.note: 1464: Famagusta returns to the kingdom (bridging). The Famagusta page says Genoa seized the port in 1372 and Venice in 1489 and is silent on the return; the Kingdom of Cyprus dynasty table starts James II's reign in 1464. Year, and that it was Genoa who gave it up, are the researcher's bridging judgment and need a page.
1489: Queen Catherine Cornaro sells Cyprus to Venice and the kingdom ends. Infobox 'Disestablished: 1489'; lead: she 'was forced to sell the island to Venice'; table: her reign ends 26 February 1489.

wars.name: Richard I's conquest of Cyprus (Third Crusade)
belligerents: the island's previous rulers (the page excerpt names no opponent)

zones.text: the island of Cyprus, conquered by Richard I in 1191

wars.outcome: Richard I conquered the island in 1191, sold it to the Knights Templar for 100,000 bezants, and after the Templars were expelled in an Easter 1192 uprising offered it to Guy of Lusignan; the Kingdom of Cyprus dates from 1192.
wars.note: Before the state's own life; listed because it is the founding.

wars.name: Genoese seizure of Famagusta
wars.outcome: 'In 1372 the port was seized by Genoa'; the infobox calls the kingdom a tributary state of Genoa 1372-1426 (citation needed).
wars.note: The war that led to it (a 1373-74 Genoese war in other accounts) is not on either page opened, so only the seizure is recorded. No contest events: the pages date no fighting.

wars.name: Mamluk campaigns against Cyprus
wars.outcome: The lead: 'The Mameluks then made the kingdom a tributary state in 1426'; the peasant-revolt paragraph mentions 'the capture of King Janus'. Infobox: 'Tributary state of the Mamluk Sultanate (1426-1489)'. No land changed hands.
wars.note: The tributary relation is carried by the mamluk-sultanate dossier (vassal_start 1426, vassal_end 1489, counterpart kingdom-of-cyprus). The 1425 start year is from that dossier's Mamluk-page reading; this page dates only 1426.

certainty.note: The island's coast is its border, so the main shape is sharp. The Anatolian ports (Antalya, Corycus, 1361-1373 and 1361-1448) and the Genoese enclave at Famagusta (1372 to the bridging year 1464) are city districts whose extent no page gives; their radii are approximate.

notes:
Cliopatria 'Kingdom of Cyprus' 1192-1491, three shapes (island 1192-1362, island plus Anatolian coast 1363-1486, island 1487-1491). Two pages opened (the budget). Verdicts: 1192 adjust (ends 1360), 1363 wrong (belongs to 1361-1371; Antalya was lost in 1373 and Corycus in 1448, but Cliopatria keeps the coast to 1486), 1487 adjust (kingdom ends 1489, not 1491); five new keyframes (1361, 1372, 1373, 1448, 1464). No infobox area on the page, so no area comparison could be made; Cliopatria's 11,437 km2 for the island shape exceeds the island's land area because it includes coastal cells.
Open: (1) the return of Famagusta from Genoa is on neither page; the 1464 gain and the 1464 keyframe are confidence-1 bridging and need a page (James II of Cyprus; Genoese Famagusta). (2) The page says nothing of a 1373-74 Genoese war, so no contest events are written. (3) The counterparts of the Anatolian ports (Teke for Antalya, Armenian Cilicia for Corycus in 1361, Ramadanid for Corycus in 1448) are readings from Cliopatria neighbours, not from the page: the lead's years carry a citation-needed tag, and who took the ports is for the Teke, Karaman, Ramadanid and Cilicia dossiers to confirm. (4) Tributary relations listed in the infobox (Armenian Cilicia 1198-1229, Holy Roman Empire 1229-1268, Genoa 1372-1426, Mamluk 1426-1489), all citation-needed, are the suzerains' to record; only the Mamluk one is already in the mamluk-sultanate dossier. (5) Templar Cyprus (1191-1192) has no Cliopatria row and no dossier. (6) Gazetteer lacks the place 'Corycus' (Korykos, Gorigos, near Kizkalesi, about 34.15 E 36.46 N, Mersin Province, Turkey). (7) The ruler list is the page's dynasty table; Louis and Catherine are named as the table gives them (Catherine is Catherine Cornaro from the lead).
